programme.title: Beyond the screen: how “film ” tourism and AI redefine moviegoer experience
programme.desc: As the Beijing International Film Festival takes over the city, films are no longer just something we watch in cinemas. They’re connecting tourism, retail, entertainment, and even cutting-edge tech. What does this “film plus” experience look like for audiences today? And as AI reshapes the film industry, what opportunities and challenges lie ahead? Host Xu Yawen spoke with Li Lun, assistant professor of economics at Peking University; Geng Ling, film producer and CEO of China Film Assist Company; and Teng Jimeng, associate professor of American studies at Beijing Foreign Studies University, to delve into these questions.

programme.title: What can Africa learn from China’s poverty reduction experience?
programme.desc: Five years after China eliminated absolute poverty, its development experience continues to attract attention around the world, particularly across Africa. What lessons can African countries draw from China’s journey? Can China’s poverty reduction experiences be adapted to African realities? In today’s episode, we bring scholars, journalists and development practitioners from China, The Gambia, Rwanda and Namibia. Jainaba Sonko, Zhang Yanqiu, Patrick Rurangangabo and Jeronimo Kateya explore pathways to sustainable development and poverty reduction, discussing governance, infrastructure, education, self-reliance and the future of China-Africa cooperation.

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc:
China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.
In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging "AI tourism" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: How rafting helped one village find new life
programme.desc: In Sankengtan Village, Guangdong Province, a river that once flowed quietly through everyday life is now part of the Gulong Gorge rafting course—a global destination drawing millions of visitors each year. What was once a quiet rural community has been transformed by tourism, as local residents build new livelihoods around the river and the opportunities it brings. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN's Vivienne Nunis joins those braving the white water to find out more.

programme.title: RAZOR: Fighting Forest Fires
programme.desc: As the planet warms, scientists predict that extreme forest fires could increase globally by up to 50% by the end of the century. Europe — the world's fastest-warming continent — is already seeing this trend, and the risk is no longer confined to the south. Razor's Gabrielle Lawrence travels to Germany, one of Europe's most heavily forested countries, to visit a region severely affected by wildfires. But can we detect a fire before it even begins to spread? A team of scientists from Dryad Networks in Germany is pioneering an AI-powered early detection system designed to identify wildfires in their earliest stages. At their test site near Eberswalde, they demonstrate how their technology can spot danger before flames take hold — during a carefully controlled burn.

programme.title: RAZOR Conversations: Quantum Leap
programme.desc: Quantum computers are moving from theory into real-world applications. In this episode of Razor, Neil Cairns meets Dr. Richard Murray, co-founder of ORCA Computing, to explore how photonic quantum computers use single particles of light as quantum bits, and why they could eventually outperform classical computers on complex problems. From energy and healthcare to chemistry and logistics, discover how quantum computing could transform the way we solve some of the world’s most challenging problems.

programme.title: CGTN & UN Tourism ｜Exploring China’s New Tourism Frontier
programme.desc: This summer, inbound tourism in China continues to boom, with nearly 23 million inbound trips by foreign nationals recorded in the first half of this year. The growth has been supported in part by expanded visa-free access, more convenient transit policies and continued improvements in tourism services. At the same time, rural tourism is playing an increasingly important role in China’s rural revitalization strategy. Join us on BizTalk for insights from UN Tourism and China Agricultural University as we explore China’s rural tourism model, the strong recovery in inbound travel and the next phase of growth for the country’s tourism industry.

programme.title: Land of Diversity
programme.desc: The power of evolution prevails even in some of the world's toughest environments. From mammals and reptiles to flowers and leafy plants, the Himalayas have some of the world's most diverse ecosystems, which have bred the most incredible diversity of life on the planet.

programme.title: From Island Farms to Cloud Power, From Mountain Hubs to Urban Beats
programme.desc: From tropical coffee aromas to high-tech computing hubs, how is China defining "high-quality development"? In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the fields of Wanning, Hainan, where a small coffee bean becomes a symbol of the Free Trade Port’s opening-up, to the mountains of Guizhou, where a 14-millisecond data latency is powering the rendering of global blockbusters like Ne Zha 2. Finally, we dive into the vibrant Livehouse scene of China’s megacities, exploring a $1.2 billion "emotional economy" that is reshaping urban nightlife. From solid digital infrastructure to the rhythmic energy of the music scene, this episode captures the heartbeat of China’s evolving economic future.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Europe's heating up: So where is the AC?
programme.desc: CGTN reporter Li Jianhua reports on how Londoners live without air conditioning, despite the British summers getting longer and heater.

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programme.desc:
Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy.
We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations.
One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programme.title: China's rural CEO experiment: How a Dai village is reinventing itself
programme.desc:
During the Dai New Year, CGTN reporter Lincoln Humphries visited Manluanzhan, a traditional Dai village near China's southwestern border in Yunnan Province.
There, "sleeping" assets are being awakened: an abandoned water tower has been turned into a café, and traditional Dai houses have been expanded to offer new types of homestays.
At the center of this experiment is an unusual figure — a rural CEO who helps balance economic development with the Dai community's traditions as the village charts its own path forward.
In this episode of #BizFocus, Lincoln Humphries shows how a village in Xishuangbanna brings fresh vitality and authentic traditions together.

programme.title: The new keeper of the ancient village in the deep mountains
programme.desc: Deep in the mountains of Fujian, Yanxiang village is home to centuries-old Hakka architecture and an aging population. But a post 1995-born returnee is giving the ancient village a new future. Follow CGTN’s He Jingyi to see how a young village chief blends modern ideas with traditional heritage, breathing new life into this millennium-old rural settlement. #BizFocus

programme.title: Observing Europe-Europe's heating up: So where is the AC?
programme.desc: CGTN reporter Li Jianhua reports on how Londoners live without air conditioning, despite the British summers getting longer and heater.

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc:
China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.
In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging "AI tourism" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: No Power, No AI
programme.desc: Is energy the ultimate bottleneck for artificial intelligence? As compute demand skyrockets, can our power grids keep up? Tune in as global leaders tackle the energy challenge powering the next wave of AI. #SummerDavos2026

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programme.desc:
Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy.
We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations.
One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programme.title: No Power, No AI
programme.desc: Is energy the ultimate bottleneck for artificial intelligence? As compute demand skyrockets, can our power grids keep up? CGTN's Michael Wang moderates a critical panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum on the intersection of AI and energy infrastructure. We'll explore how to align capital investment, infrastructure build-out, and policy frameworks; future-proof energy supply systems to strengthen energy security; and build a more inclusive, sustainable AI-powered energy future. Tune in as global leaders tackle the energy challenge powering the next wave of AI. #SummerDavos2026

programme.title: Who owns Britain?
programme.desc:
One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely.
It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners.
For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned.
In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Why China's theme parks are having a moment

programme.title: Who owns Britain?
programme.desc:
One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely.
It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners.
For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned.
In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.desc: This summer, inbound tourism in China continues to boom, with nearly 23 million inbound trips by foreign nationals recorded in the first half of this year. At the same time, rural tourism is playing an increasingly important role in China’s rural revitalization strategy. Join us on BizTalk for insights from UN Tourism and China Agricultural University as we explore China’s rural tourism model, the strong recovery in inbound travel and the next phase of growth for the country’s tourism industry.

programme.title: China Popcast: All you need to know for traveling in China this summer
programme.desc: Traveling in China for the first time can be a little easier if you know a few things beforehand. In this episode of China Popcast, we tell you which maps to use, how to pay for things, offer advice on how to book tickets for major attractions, share information on China's current travel visa policies and more. Our guests Chen Hongpeng, a Beijing-based tour guide, and CGTN China Travel host Jack Klumpp join the show to give you expert tips for your China trip this summer. And new China Popcast host Min Rui gets the show going with quickfire questions on the "dos and don'ts."

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum-0
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Life in Camel Town
programme.desc: When it comes to Mongolian, most people will think of grasslands, horse racing. In fact, the camel is the king of five livestock of nomadic people. Camel is the meritorious?figure in the vast desert on the Silk Road. In this episode, we go to Alashan: Camel Town in China, to experience the life of Mongolian people and camels in desert. Milking, delivering milk and collecting camels, also has a thrilling journey to pick up the newborn baby camel. We deeply feel the profound feeling between the camel raiser and their camels.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor-worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people’s positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Three Gorges of Chongqing
programme.desc: In this episode, through the new fashion of five-star cruise tour on the Three Gorges, with comfortable and convenient high-end experiences, we take the audience to travel along the river, multi-dimensionally show the most spectacular and beautiful landscape gallery along the Yangtze River, feel the unique charm of canyons, rapids and cultural relics on both banks, and convey the new charm of Yangtze River cultural tourism.

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum-0
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: China Bound：Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor-worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people’s positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Three Gorges of Chongqing
programme.desc: In this episode, through the new fashion of five-star cruise tour on the Three Gorges, with comfortable and convenient high-end experiences, we take the audience to travel along the river, multi-dimensionally show the most spectacular and beautiful landscape gallery along the Yangtze River, feel the unique charm of canyons, rapids and cultural relics on both banks, and convey the new charm of Yangtze River cultural tourism.

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum-0
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: Foodwise: Changsha
programme.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May embark on a journey to Changsha in Hunan Province.?They taste their way through the local cuisine, discover the city's latest art and fashion trends, and find out why this place is one of China's "influencer hotspots", attracting millions of domestic and foreign tourists each year.

programme.title: Foodwise：Qingdao
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"

programme.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China’s most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang’s First Peak – this time, he’s all in.

programme.title: Village Voyage: Before the icon Bruce Lee, there was Shunde in Foshan-0
programme.desc: Nunchucks. Dark shades. A yellow jumpsuit. That unmistakable nose wipe. Blinding punches and the snake feint – one name says it all: Bruce Lee, the man who brought Chinese martial arts to the world. But every legend has a beginning – and his is less well known. It started in Shunde of Foshan City, south China's Guangdong Province. Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: China's Ancient “Wall Street”: Pingyao
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Pingyao – the ancient "Wall Street" of China and a historic banking hub. Enclosed by ancient city walls and seemingly frozen in time, this entire city, together with two nearby ancient temples, offers a one-of-a-kind adventure at this UNESCO World Heritage Site!

programme.title: Colors of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In the first episode of our Sichuan Daliang Mountains series, we journey to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province. Setting off from Xichang, the prefectural capital, we first explore Lizhou Ancient Town, the southern gateway of the Southern Silk Road. We then travel to Huili County in the southernmost part of the Daliang Mountains, where we listen to the morning bells and evening drums, try our hand at making green pottery, and pick fresh pomegranates. Finally, we head to the western part of the Greater Liangshan Mountains and step into the mysterious Lugu Lake. We visit a Mosuo family to learn about their unique culture and take part in one of the Mosuo people’s most important rituals: the coming?of?age ceremony.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Navigating the Hills of Chongqing
programme.desc: This episode explores the transportation ingenuity of Chongqing, the Fog City. Surrounded by mountains and rivers, this megacity solves topographic challenges with the Yangtze River Cableway, Asia's second-longest escalator, and a train passing through a building. From the dock culture at the confluence of two rivers to a logistics hub linking China and Europe, witness its transformation from an inland town to an economic center via the Go West policy.

programme.title: Fiery Tales of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In this episode, our host takes you to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province, to celebrate the most traditional Torch Festival with the local Yi people. Water nourishes the farmland; fire brings light and warmth. Water and fire are the two essential elements that sustain the life of the Yi people. Puge County is known as the birthplace of the Yi Torch Festival. Our host travels across mountains to the remote heart of Puge County, in search of the origins of the Yi torch, to learn about local daily life, explore the profound Yi culture, and visit a Yi family to share a special “reunion dinner” on the eve of the Torch Festival—just like their own New Year's Eve feast. Together with the locals, we celebrate their most magnificent festival: the Torch Festival.

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu

After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: Foodwise: Quanzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in Quanzhou, the ancient starting point of the Maritime Silk Road. From its covered arcades and Roman columns to its Southeast Asian vibe, our hosts discover that Quanzhou truly is a melting pot of world cultures. Then there’s the food: From the local noodle porridge that utilizes Silk Road spices, to fried vinegar pork and a dessert made from a special algae, there’s plenty of unique dishes to try here. Over a cup of oolong, our hosts will discover how Quanzhou’s tea changed the world, and how trade with Arab civilizations influenced a local fishing village. So join us in Quanzhou, a city that UNESCO designated as an “Emporium of the World”!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xi'an
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Xi'an, an ancient city with over 3000 years of history, capital to 13 Chinese dynasties. But first, our hosts are going to carb load on street food, from glutinous rice cakes and cakes made out of persimmons, to mutton soup with flatbread and the famous biangbiang noodles. They'll also taste the rich history of Xi'an by experiencing a Qin Dynasty-inspired banquet, and try millennia-old dishes such as trout grilled on a ceramic tile and calabash chicken, a Tang Dynasty delicacy. From the Terracotta Army to the Daming Palace, residence of the Tang emperors, to a dazzling nighttime boulevard that recreates the grandeur of the Tang Dynasty, there's so much to explore in Xi'an. So, get your camera and your stomach ready for CGTN's Foodwise in Xi'an!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: China Bound: Chongqing
programme.desc: Join us in southwest China's Chongqing, one of the world's biggest cities. From futuristic skylines and cyberpunk streets, to fire-breathing opera, spicy hotpot and kungfu tea, we're diving deep into this megacity the size of Austria.

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program "China Untapped: Suzhou" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou’s high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou’s urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou’s industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: Shunde's flavors: where tradition blends with vivid daily life
programme.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures – from crispy fish skin to fried milk – into culinary wonders. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia, are setting out to taste the flavors and feel the warmth of Shunde's countryside with the locals.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha — the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Our lens turns to the "Xiangjiang Ladies" who work in Changsha’s high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city’s innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha’s distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: Tasting the Lifestyle of Chongqing
programme.desc: This episode uncovers Chongqing's lifestyle, where hot pot is more than food but a city symbol intertwined with climate and history. Tracing its roots at a hot pot museum and experiencing mountain restaurants, we see its evolution from dockworkers' fare to a trendy lifestyle. Exploring graffiti streets, old teahouses and Hongyadong, we find Chongqing balances vibrancy and leisure amid modern development.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Tasting the Lifestyle of Chongqing
programme.desc: This episode uncovers Chongqing's lifestyle, where hot pot is more than food but a city symbol intertwined with climate and history. programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: China Bound: Guangzhou
programme.desc: Join us in Guangzhou, a global manufacturing hub in south China with a population as large as New York’s. From browsing hip street markets to wholesale clothes shopping, sampling world-famous Cantonese cuisine, and visiting the childhood home of kungfu legend Bruce Lee, there is plenty to do during our stay.

programme.title: Dance of Heroes
programme.desc: In this episode, our host “Uncle Hanzi” travels to Chaonan in Shantou to explore the story of a family devoted to the tradition of Yingge dance. Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father’s dedication, his daughter’s passion, and his apprentices’ enthusiasm—showcasing how this centuries-old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: My Little Cricket Fighter
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore a time-honored form of entertainment in China that has existed for thousands of years – cricket fighting. Music, Chinese chess, calligraphy and painting, and raising flowers, birds, fish and insects are known as the Eight Traditional Pastimes of the Chinese people. Raising insects may be the last on the list, but it is a pastime unique to China. Though these small creatures are tiny, the culture surrounding them has been nurtured by the Chinese people over thousands of years, embodying the unique cultural psychology, folk customs and aesthetic values of the Chinese nation.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.1: Old Gems
programme.desc: Xiamen, a key starting point of China’s ancient Maritime Silk Road, is one of China’s most livable cities. In this episode, host Min-Zhui Lee and co-host Pan William, an honorary citizen of Xiamen and a professor, take you on an immersive journey through the city. Explore Xiamen University, renowned as China’s most beautiful university campus, and visit Wanshi Park, known as “China’s First Lawn”. Trace Xiamen’s history through its streets, admiring the arcades that tell the stories of the city’s early commercial development. Finally, board a boat to Gulangyu Islet, the “Island of Music” — the birthplace of modern music education in China, and a living “World Architecture Museum”. Every corner of this islet lets you experience the past and present of Xiamen’s vibrant life.

Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father’s dedication, his daughter’s passion, and his apprentices’ enthusiasm—showcasing how this centuries-old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: My Little Cricket Fighter
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore a time-honored form of entertainment in China that has existed for thousands of years – cricket fighting. Music, Chinese chess, calligraphy and painting, and raising flowers, birds, fish and insects are known as the Eight Traditional Pastimes of the Chinese people. Raising insects may be the last on the list, but it is a pastime unique to China. Though these small creatures are tiny, the culture surrounding them has been nurtured by the Chinese people over thousands of years, embodying the unique cultural psychology, folk customs and aesthetic values of the Chinese nation.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.1: Old Gems
programme.desc: Xiamen, a key starting point of China’s ancient Maritime Silk Road, is one of China’s most livable cities. In this episode, host Min-Zhui Lee and co-host Pan William, an honorary citizen of Xiamen and a professor, take you on an immersive journey through the city. Explore Xiamen University, renowned as China’s most beautiful university campus, and visit Wanshi Park, known as “China’s First Lawn”. Trace Xiamen’s history through its streets, admiring the arcades that tell the stories of the city’s early commercial development. Finally, board a boat to Gulangyu Islet, the “Island of Music” — the birthplace of modern music education in China, and a living “World Architecture Museum”. Every corner of this islet lets you experience the past and present of Xiamen’s vibrant life.

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: White Crane
programme.desc: In Yongchun, China, Kleber explores the origins of White Crane kungfu and its effect on the martial arts world. He learns how its blocks and strikes were inspired by animal movements, and how acupuncture points can be used to deadly effect. After training his grip and finger strength with wooden sticks, he travels to Beijing for an introduction to Goju-ryu karate, and discovers striking similarities with White Crane.

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: "When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes. In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadic life."

programme.title: The secret of the 'Long Hair' village
programme.desc: For the Red Yao women of Guangxi, southern China, hair is far more than a mark of beauty – it's a living narrative of identity, lineage, and nature. Each stage of life is reflected in how they wear it, carrying the memory of their families and the wisdom of their ancestors. Their time-honored rice-water hair care ritual is not just a beauty secret – it's a thread connecting generations, preserving ecological knowledge passed down through centuries. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they step into Huangluo Yao Village, known as the "World's Longest Hair Village," to uncover the stories and traditions behind the Red Yao's legendary long hair.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Silversmith
programme.desc: In this episode, Eva May steps into Maliao Village — a century-old silversmith village nestled in Leishan, Guizhou Province. Over the course of a week, she dives into the craft and daily lives of Miao men who carry on the silversmithing legacy. She works side by side with local silversmiths day in and day out, delving into the culture and techniques behind Miao silverware. She even joins master silversmiths for a live-stream event, before engaging in discussions with university professors about how traditional craftsmanship can fuel rural revitalization. On top of that, she witnesses the breathtaking sight of "maidens adorned in silver and flowers" at the grand Miao New Year celebrations, visits Xijiang Qianhu Miaozhai — the world’s largest Miao village — and learns to forge a small yet meaningful piece of Miao silver ornament.

programme.title: Inner Mongolia’s Frozen Wonderland
programme.desc: In this episode, we feature the Winter Nadam Fair and winter sports in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia. By late December, the Hulunbuir Grassland is blanketed in ice and snow. Even in the bitter cold of around 30 degrees below zero, the grassland is alive with a festive bustle.

programme.title: Fun Guide to China: Hainan 1
programme.desc: As Hainan moves towards implementing its special customs operation, CGTN’s Travelogue is launching a brand-new series, “Fun Guide to China”. Set in Hainan, the pilot episode journeys through its cities, mountains, coastlines and rainforests, capturing the vibrant atmosphere of life in the Free Trade Port.From the world’s largest stand-alone duty-free mall – a true shopper’s paradise, to the laid-back charm of an “Old Dad Tea” restaurant, host Tianran He explores the evolving cityscape of Haikou. On the northeast coast in Wenchang, he joins a local photographer to witness the launch of a Chinese space rocket, before diving into interactive space museums that bring the cosmos within reach. The journey then heads west to Danzhou, where campervans and “mermaids” share the same stage, before reaching Wanning on the east coast, where Tianran catches waves at one of China’s most famous surfing hotspots.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.2: New Jewels
programme.desc: In the second episode of our Xiamen series, host Tianran He and co-host Laura, an American who has lived in Xiamen for 7 years, guide you to discover Xiamen's internationalization, modernization, and unique fashion vibe. First, they cycle along the island road, taking in the stunning coastal scenery of the famous Round-the-Island Road, and step into Zengcuoan — once a small fishing village, now a thriving creative hub — to showcase its remarkable transformation. Next, Laura leads Tianran to experience the daily life of expats in Xiamen: exploring the lively coffee bar street, and joining a fun gathering at a stylish French restaurant. A passionate lover of Chinese culture, Laura invites Tianran to experience a traditional Chinese tea ceremony. After that, the pair head to Xiamen’s fashion central business district, experimenting with bold new looks in clothing stores that have caught the eye of the global fashion community. Finally, Tianran visits an egret habitat to meet photographers who document these beautiful birds, and together they admire the grace of Xiamen's iconic egrets.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: "When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes. In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadic life."

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan’s explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of “opening the gate”, the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou’s rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: Celadon Ou Music
programme.desc: Celadon ou music is also called "bowl music.” The reason is that the ancient Chinese word for bowl sounds like ou. The music originated simply as improvised rhythms tapped out on bowls. It was this spontaneity that made celadon ou so popular. Celadon ou music was at the height of its popularity over 1,100 years ago. But with time, it faded from history. At one point, it was even on the verge of being lost forever. After hundreds of years of obscurity, it re-emerged at the end of last century.

programme.title: Clothing woven in the mountains
programme.desc: "In Longsheng, southern China, ethnic communities have lived for generations among the same mountains and rivers. The landscape of terraced fields stretches across the valleys, carrying layered cultural memories. In this episode, CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipino singer Eliza Arce travel to Huangluo Yao Village. Beginning with the Red Yao tradition of sun-drying clothes, they explore the colours, craftsmanship, and everyday wisdom woven into these garments. Their journey culminates in a vibrant bonfire gathering, where different communities come together in celebration."

programme.title: New Year with the Miao
programme.desc: In this episode, it’s Miao New Year, and that means multitudes of merrymaking! Fishing, drinking, bullfighting… Join the host Min-Zhui Lee, among the magnificent mountains of Leishan, where it’s all happening for the ethnic Miao.

programme.title: Exploring the Long Winter
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Jingpo Lake, Xuexiang and Yabuli in Mudanjiang, showcasing the unique winter ice fishing festival, the fairytale-like scenery of Xuexiang, and its world-class ski resorts.

programme.title: Fun Guide to China: Hainan 2
programme.desc: In this episode host Tianran He continues his adventure across Hainan. This time, the road trip begins in Dongfang, where Tianran tucks into roast suckling pig by day and, by night, attends grassroots basketball games that rival NBA games in atmosphere. In the mountains of Wuzhishan, Tianran explores a lush jungle with forest rangers, before stepping back in time to 1988 for a retro-chic disco night. In Lingshui, the journey moves offshore as Tianran enjoys a seafood feast on a floating fishing platform, then heads back to shore to visit a contemporary art museum by the pier. After reaching Sanya in the south, he joins scuba divers on a mission to restore coral reefs, before winding down on a yacht with friends and laughter. Finally, Tianran travels to Baisha for the “La’aomen” harvest festival, where the local ethnic Li people sing, dance and celebrate their most important crop: “Mountain Orchid Rice”.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.3
programme.desc: In the third episode of our Xiamen series, we introduce four expats from BRICS countries and their inspiring lives in Xiamen. Bjorn, from South Africa, is deeply passionate about Chinese food culture and architecture, and is even skilled at oracle bone script calligraphy. Living in Shapowei, Xiamen’s busiest creative district, he knows every street and lane intimately, and has a profound love for the city's charm. Atul Verma, a yoga teacher from India, opened a yoga studio in Xiamen and built a new career here. Surrounded by Xiamen's peaceful Buddhist atmosphere, he has found a true sense of home in this foreign land. Juan Guimaraes, from Brazil, is an international freshman studying medicine at Xiamen University. Filled with curiosity and longing for both the campus and the city, he hopes to live a fulfilling life at the university and fall in love with Xiamen. Rustam Apushev, from Russia, is known to everyone as a loving “super dad”, but his true identity is a former boxing champion with countless championship medals. He met his wife in Xiamen, raised two children, founded his own school, and started a whole new life. “Xiamen is my home,” he says."
